_doc: EwokOS capability policy for machine.virt (QEMU virt, arm/aarch64).
Read by /sbin/init, which pushes every entry into the kernel's
exec-time policy via SYS_CAP_POLICY_ADD. The kernel then grants a
rule's caps by itself whenever an image whose cmd (first token of
procinfo.cmd) matches the rule execs - process-start order and
restarts are irrelevant. With a policy file present, init runs the
boot scripts as uid 1 so these caps are what actually authorizes
the services; without it, scripts run as root like before.
Entry forms:
{"type":"root"                                                   "rights":"rwxg"}
{"type":"frame", "paddr":"0x...", "size":"0x...", "rights":"rw"}
{"type":"dma",   "block":0,                       "rights":"rw"}
rights letters: r=read, w=write, x=execute, g=grant (forwardable).
QEMU virt layout notes:
- MMIO window 0x08000000..0x0c000000 (64MB). Drivers map only the
sub-regions below via mmio_map_offset(), so frame caps are scoped
per device instead of covering the whole window.
- PL011 UART0 @0x09000000 (one page), irq 33.
- fw_cfg @0x09020000 (one page), used by ramfb setup.
- virtio-mmio @0x0a000000, 32 slots x 0x200 = 0x4000, irqs 48+i;
the configured range 48..55 covers the first 8 slots. Virtqueues
and data buffers come from dma_user_alloc() (dma block 0).

rules.desc: soft-timer service: sends soft irqs to clients (irq number not examined)
2d blit engine: peer-maps client dma canvases
setuid boundary: switches uid/gid after auth (setuid-root equivalent)
